body:
selfhost/emit.prn now constructs a new struct value from a map literal ({:x expr :y expr}), the other of the two gaps flagged since defstruct support first landed. Scoped narrow: only a defn whose entire body is a struct literal matching its own declared struct return type. Emits a real C99 compound literal, not the reference's own Point_new(...) constructor-function convention. Found and fixed a real live type mismatch: Option-Node/deref lookups repeatedly failed real gcc compiles since deref needs a concrete declared type to hook into -- redesigned around plain I32 indexes instead. Also fixed a second real gap: a mismatched literal used to fall through to a generic return-with-no-value compile error instead of this file's own established named #error convention. 7 new tests including a real compile+run+assert check with deliberately reordered map-literal keys, plus a negative test. Zero regressions: 336-test suite + all 6 selfhost domains + bazel build/test clean. PARENA commit 7d1ba5e.

⚓ ☃
title: Self-hosted compiler: real struct-literal construction, closing the defstruct gap pair
